name: Rook Anand-Mbeki
description: A Shelf-born muralist and spoken-word broadcaster operating out of the collapsed transit tunnels beneath Old Milwaukee Station, Rook Anand-Mbeki has never accepted a corporate sponsorship and has turned down three documented buyout offers from HelixMedia Corp. Her neural-feed broadcasts — raw, unedited, transmitted through pirated BCI relay nodes — document the daily texture of Tier 1 survival: ghost market raids, improvised surgery, the smell of recycled protein paste. She paints directly onto the Shelf's structural bones, her murals layered so thick they've become load-bearing in some sections.
cultural_impact: Her phrase 'the wall remembers what the feed deletes' has become a Shelf rallying cry, stenciled in hundreds of locations across GLMZ's lower tiers. Tier 3 and 4 users who follow her illegally do so with a specific shame-adjacent thrill — she knows they're watching and addresses them directly and without warmth.
locations: The Slab — a 400m stretch of painted corridor, Shelf District 7
story_hooks: One of Rook's murals has been partially demolished by a HelixMedia construction crew — but the section they destroyed contained a hidden encoded message that only reveals itself in the rubble pattern, and someone is trying to decode it before the rubble is cleared.
A Tier 4 art collector has purchased a section of wall Rook painted — legally, through a building acquisition — and wants to move it to a private gallery. Rook has promised consequences.

Rook's latest broadcast went dark mid-transmission. Her relay technician Dust hasn't been seen in four days, and her followers are organizing a search that could expose dozens of illegal BCI relay nodes.
platform: Pirated BCI relay broadcast (no registered platform)
follower_count: ~340,000 Shelf-local; estimated 1.2M including Tier 2-4 illegal subscribers
controversy: In 2219, she broadcast the face and home address of a HelixMedia executive whose demolition order displaced 800 Shelf residents. The executive was not harmed, but the broadcast triggered a corponation-level suppression order that took eight months to partially enforce.
